scenes.anchor_text: It was a Tuesday, and the calendar had just ticked over to January 3rd. A terrible winter storm had descended on North America, and half the country was buried in snow and ice. In Seattle we didn’t have too much snow that night. But it was well below zero, which was unusually cold, even for January.
scenes.scene_description: A desolate, frigid Seattle street at night, a light dusting of snow covers the ground, emphasizing the biting cold and emptiness. The scene showcases the unusually harsh winter conditions mentioned in the text, focusing on the stillness and quiet of the late hour.

scenes.anchor_text: Me, I didn’t have a choice. Like I said, it was below freezing. I was outside. And I was wearing boxers, a leather jacket, and a pair of pink Crocs sandals that barely fit me.
scenes.scene_description: A disheveled figure stands shivering in the cold night air, illuminated by a nearby streetlight. He is scantily clad in boxers, a leather jacket, and pink Crocs. His posture reflects discomfort and regret.

scenes.anchor_text: I was also holding a crying, scratching, squirming, and spitting cat named Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk. She was a tortoiseshell, Persian cat worth more than I made in a year. My ex-girlfriend called her Princess Donut for short. I just stuck with Donut.
scenes.scene_description: The man awkwardly holds a struggling tortoiseshell Persian cat in his arms, the cat's distress is evident. The scene highlights the reluctant bond between the man and the valuable feline.

scenes.anchor_text: She jumped up on my shoulder, and she leaped out the second-story window onto the tree outside my apartment. Just like that. I’d had that window open dozens of times over the past year, and she’d never even given the window a second glance.
scenes.scene_description: A fluffy Persian cat leaps from a second-story window onto a snow-covered tree branch in the dead of night. The apartment building is dimly lit in the background, hinting at the warmth left behind.
scenes.image_prompt: Cinematic digital painting, Persian cat leaping from window to tree branch, Second-story apartment window, dark and cold winter night, muted tones with dramatic contrasts, soft lighting emanating from the window, medium shot capturing the cat's leap, Donut: Tortoiseshell Persian cat, mid-air, determined

scenes.anchor_text: So instead, she decided to start howling at the top of her lungs. I spent the next several minutes cursing at the cat, trying to coax her back inside. I opened the window all the way, sending gales of ice-cold air in the previously-toasty apartment.
scenes.scene_description: The man leans out the open second-story window, desperately trying to coax a howling cat perched on a tree branch. The cold air billows out of the window into the night.

scenes.anchor_text: I rushed down the stairs, and I jumped outside, rushing to the tree that sat between the sidewalk and the building. I immediately regretted not taking the time to put proper clothes on. The cold, windy air sunk its claws into my legs and feet.
scenes.scene_description: The man exits the apartment building and rushes toward a tree, his bare legs exposed to the frigid winter air. The scene emphasizes the biting cold and his immediate regret.

scenes.anchor_text: “What in god’s name is going on out here?” Mrs. Parsons called, sticking her head out the window. The old woman had her head wrapped in a some sort of towel, making her look like a swami. Her beady eyes focused on me. “Carl, is that you?”
scenes.scene_description: An elderly woman with her head wrapped in a towel peers out of a first-floor apartment window, questioning the man standing outside in the cold.
scenes.image_prompt: Cinematic digital painting, Elderly woman peering out of a window, First-floor apartment window, cold and dark night, muted tones with dramatic contrasts, soft lighting from the apartment interior, medium shot focusing on the woman's face and the window, Mrs. Parsons: Elderly woman, head wrapped in a towel, beady eyes

scenes.anchor_text: The building smashed down to the ground. I watched it happen. The seven-story apartment building was there one moment, and then it was gone. But it hadn’t disappeared. I was looking right at Mrs. Parsons when it went down.
scenes.scene_description: A seven-story apartment building is instantly crushed to the ground in a catastrophic event, dust and debris fill the air. A silhouette of a man stands in the foreground witnessing the destruction.

scenes.anchor_text: Everything was gone except the trees and the bicycles in the bike racks, and Marjory Williams’s moped that was still booted by parking enforcement.
scenes.scene_description: A scene of surreal destruction where only trees, a bike rack with bicycles, and a booted moped remain amidst the flattened landscape. The scene conveys the randomness and bizarre nature of the event.

scenes.anchor_text: All that remained of my building was a rectangle of churned dirt and rocks. And then I saw it, right near my feet. It was Mrs. Parson’s head. In the dark, it was hard to discern. But I immediately knew what it was.
scenes.scene_description: A rectangle of churned dirt marks where the apartment building once stood. In the foreground, a severed head lies amidst the debris, barely visible in the darkness.
scenes.image_prompt: Cinematic digital painting, Rectangle of churned dirt and severed head, Seattle street after destruction, muted tones with dramatic contrasts, dark and somber lighting, close-up focusing on the grim discovery, no characters visible

scenes.anchor_text: Then came the voice. A male, robotic voice. It spoke in my mind. The voice was like a physical thing. A spike in my brain, scratching me. It wasn’t speaking English. But I understood the words. As the person spoke, the text also appeared floating in front of me.
scenes.scene_description: A disoriented man stands in the ruined landscape, looking up at floating alien text that appears before him. The scene emphasizes the bizarre and incomprehensible nature of the communication.

scenes.anchor_text: Less than a hundred feet to my left, right in the middle of what had once been a thrift store, a spotlight burst into the air. I saw an additional spotlight appear about a mile away. I turned, and I saw a few more littered throughout the city.
scenes.scene_description: Beams of light erupt from the ruined cityscape, marking the entrances to the World Dungeon. The scene showcases the sudden and inexplicable appearance of these gateways.
scenes.image_prompt: Cinematic digital painting, Spotlights bursting from ruins of city, Seattle landscape after destruction, muted tones with dramatic contrasts, intense spotlights illuminating the sky, wide shot capturing the spread of the spotlights, no characters visible

scenes.anchor_text: So I turned toward the light, and I ran.
